body: Microinverter maker trading below ~$1 in 2016-17 with going-concern-type worries [unverified]. Badri Kothandaraman (COO 2017, CEO Sept 2017) ran a cost/pricing/opex plan: redesigned IQ microinverters, cut costs, raised prices, refinanced debt; gross margin from ~20% to ~40%+ [unverified]. Joined S&P 500 Jan 2021. Peak ~$340 (Dec 2022) [unverified] ≈ 400x from the low. Split: loss-to-profit plus P/E up to ~100x; US residential solar boom (30% 25D tax credit, IRA 2022), California NEM 2.0. Bust: California NEM 3.0 (Apr 2023) cut payback economics, rates rose (solar loans), European distributor inventory glut 2023-24, SolarEdge-style channel destock; then the July 2025 tax law phased out the 25D credit for customer-owned systems after 2025. Stock $40.47 mid-2025 (-67% from Aug 2024's $123.65), ~$30s late 2025: ~-90% from peak [unverified]. EARLY SIGNAL (up) visible 2018: gross margin rising quarter after quarter with a new CEO's public 3-step plan, while the stock was <$5. EARLY SIGNAL (down): demand dependent on one state's net-metering rule and federal credits, plus distributor inventory rising faster than installs. Who caught it: few documented; retail/momentum. LESSON: a genuine operational turnaround can ride a policy-subsidised boom to 400x, but demand that exists because of subsidies reverses when policy and rates turn; treat as cyclical, not compounder.

data.early_signals: up: GM expansion under new CEO; down: NEM 3.0, rates, channel inventory, 25D phase-out
data.lesson: subsidy-driven demand is cyclical; policy is the hidden variable

title: Enphase 2016-2025: near-bankrupt to ~400x, then -90% bust
